explanations: RunHistoryHandler.list calls `this.store.jobsForRuns([r.id])` once per run inside `runs.map`, so a 100-run page issues 100 pipeline_jobs queries (N+1), even though jobsForRuns takes an array and can load every run's jobs in one `ANY` query. Because they run concurrently through Promise.all, a single page request can also take up to 100 pool connections at once, starving other requests. It should call jobsForRuns(runs.map(r => r.id)) once and group the rows by runId.
recentRuns clamps the limit with Math.min(limit, 100), and list compares runs.length to the same Math.min(limit, 100) when setting nextCursor. No error is raised, and the cursor is not always null.
Rows are ordered by id DESC, nextCursor is the last (smallest) id, and recentRuns adds `AND id < $3` for beforeId. It is keyset pagination, not an offset, and not timestamp-based.
summarize skips jobs with `durationMs === null`, so slowest stays null and slowestJob is null. No job is chosen by position, and the null check prevents comparing against null.
